content.title: About
content.content: Garlic sauce is a fragrant condiment made from fresh garlic, olive oil, lemon juice and spices. It is popular in Mediterranean and Asian cuisines, used as a dip, salad dressing, marinade for meat and fish, and as an addition to vegetable and potato dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The classic garlic sauce originates from Greece, where a yogurt‑free version is called “tzatziki”.
Garlic contains sulfur compounds that form aromatic allicin when crushed.
Homemade sauce can be kept in the refrigerator for up to a week and frozen for up to three months.
In some countries the sauce is served with seafood, in others with grilled meat.
Home‑made sauce usually lacks preservatives, giving it a brighter flavor than industrial versions.

items.title: Immune support
items.content: Garlic is rich in allicin and other antioxidants that may boost the body’s defense mechanisms.

items.title: Cardiovascular support
items.content: Olive oil provides monounsaturated fats that help lower LDL cholesterol.

items.title: Anti‑inflammatory action
items.content: Sulfur compounds in garlic have anti‑inflammatory properties, which can be beneficial in chronic inflammation.

items.title: Blood pressure reduction
items.content: Studies suggest regular garlic consumption may contribute to modest blood pressure lowering.

items.title: Digestive aid
items.content: Lemon juice stimulates bile production, improving fat digestion.

items.title: Garlic allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to garlic, such as skin itching or swelling.

items.title: Stomach irritation
items.content: Large amounts of raw garlic can irritate the stomach lining and cause heartburn.

items.title: Medication interactions
items.content: Garlic may enhance the effect of anticoagulants, so people on blood thinners should consult a doctor.

items.title: Bad breath
items.content: The strong aroma of garlic can linger in breath and sweat after consumption.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve garlic sauce as a dip for bread, vegetable sticks and shrimp, use it as a salad dressing, marinate chicken, fish or vegetables, or stir it into pasta and pizza for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the sauce in an airtight container in the refrigerator at 0‑4 °C. Shelf life is 7‑10 days. For longer storage, transfer to a freezer‑safe bag and keep up to 3 months. Discard if it develops off‑odors or changes color.
